Maria Sharapova’s financial journey didn’t end when she retired from professional tennis in 2020. The five-time Grand Slam champion had already amassed a large commercial profile during her playing career, with endorsements and business ventures supplementing her tennis earnings. Sharapova made $325 million before taxes during her career, which included endorsement income, Forbes reported.The most obvious example of her leap into entrepreneurship was her candy company, Sugarpova, which she founded in 2012. The venture gave Sharapova hands-on experience in branding, product development and business operations, and established the foundation for her later investing activities.Sharapova has built her wealth not just from professional tennis, but from a number of different income streams. Her Grand Slam wins have helped increase her global profile and partnerships with companies such as Nike, Evian, Porsche and TAG Heuer have generated significant commercial opportunities.Sugarpova was a big step in that Sharapova went from being a sponsored athlete to a business owner. The company eventually shut down, but the experience helped her develop an understanding of entrepreneurship and investment.With her tennis career, Sharapova’s commercial portfolio expanded. One of her most significant partnerships was with Nike, while brands such as Porsche, Evian and TAG Heuer helped boost her global commercial profile.Her work with Supergoop! was another on her path. Sharapova invested in and fronted the skincare company, blending her public profile with an ownership stake instead of simply using traditional endorsement deals.That meant Sharapova could learn about branding, product development and commercial strategy, all the while still capitalizing on her reputation as an elite athlete.Since retiring, Sharapova has shifted her focus more toward investment and advisory opportunities. She has worked with companies across wellness, fitness, beauty and fintech, including Therabody, Tonal, Supergoop!, Bala Bangles, Public.com and MoonPay.Her connection with Therabody was more than just a sponsorship. Sharapova became an investor and member of the company’s advisory board, bringing her professional athlete background to the wellness-focused business.She also appeared on Shark Tank and then partnered with Mark Cuban for an investment in Bala Bangles. Sharapova has also taken a seat on the board of luxury fashion group Moncler, adding corporate leadership to her entrepreneurial portfolio.These ventures mark a shift for Sharapova, from making money primarily. One of the most well-rounded athletes in the world, with a model that includes all through tennis and endorsements to a model that includes business ownership, investments and strategic advisory roles.Maria Sharapova has built an estimated $220 million fortune through a combination of professional tennis earnings, major endorsement deals, entrepreneurship and strategic investments. Forbes reported that she earned $325 million before taxes during her career, while partnerships with Nike, Porsche, Evian and TAG Heuer expanded her commercial reach beyond tournament prize money.
Article Summary: Maria sharapova made $325 million before taxes during her career, according to forbes. The five-time grand slam champion turned endorsements into long-term business opportunities. She has worked with companies across wellness, fitness, beauty and fintech.

Article Title: Nolan Wells murder case update: Forensic expert clarifies what happened to deleted Snapchat messages
Article Text:
Nolan Wells phone records offer a clearer picture

Deleted Snapchat messages draw fresh attention

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The mystery surrounding Nolan Wells’ phone has taken another turn after a digital forensic expert hired by the teenager’s family clarified what he meant when he previously discussed deleted messages. Andrew Garrett said Snapchat messages had been remotely recalled or deleted by their senders, but he found no evidence that someone unlocked and tampered with Wells’ phone after his disappearance. The distinction is significant because it separates deleted Snapchat content from claims that someone accessed Wells’ device.Garrett addressed the issue during a livestream published on YouTube on September 27. He explained that messages exchanged through Snapchat can be removed remotely by the person who sent them.“When we say erased from the phone, you’ve got to be a little careful with that. What happens is, when you and I are in conversation on Snapchat, and you decide to delete the messages on my side of the phone, you can do that remotely. That was done. There are some messages that were recalled and deleted from the phone,” Garrett said.He then stressed that his findings should not be interpreted as proof that someone physically accessed Wells’ device.“I didn’t say somebody unlocked the phone and started playing with the phone and started deleting the phone because that’s exactly what I would’ve said,” he added.Garrett said his examination also identified interactions with the device, such as the screen being activated, but those actions did not show that someone had unlocked it.Almost 3,000 Snapchat records from Wells’ account were released by Garrett’s forensic company. The records include group conversations in which people began raising concerns about Wells’ whereabouts on July 5.Some messages had disappeared, but the available evidence indicated they were deleted by the senders rather than by someone operating Wells’ account or phone. Garrett said Wells’ phone was last used at about 2:17 or 2:18 p.m. on July 4 and remained locked until it reached his family on July 5.The distinction has also become part of a dispute between Wells’ family and attorneys for three friends who were with him before his death. Those attorneys deny that their clients deleted messages from Wells’ phone and have disputed claims attributed to the family’s forensic examiner.Their representatives have also said they intend to sue family attorney Ben Crump for defamation.The forensic clarification does not resolve the wider questions surrounding Wells’ disappearance and death. Instead, it narrows one specific issue: deleted Snapchat messages do not, based on Garrett’s explanation, establish that someone gained access to Wells’ locked phone.
Article Summary: Digital forensic expert andrew garrett said snapchat messages had been remotely recalled or deleted by their senders. But he found no evidence that someone unlocked and tampered with wells’ phone after his disappearance. The distinction is significant because it separates deleted snapchat content from claims that someone accessed wells' device.

Article Title: Bombay HC to X: Remove video against Serum Institute, Adar Poonawalla
Article Text:
Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to take down a recent video uploaded by Yohan Tengra.





MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla that was uploaded by a social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.Justice Gauri Godse of HC on Tuesday passed the order on SII and Poonawalla’s interim application in the pending defamation suit regarding content posted against the company and its COVID-19 vaccine. She also issued show-cause notices to Tengra, his organisation Anarchy for Freedom India, Ambar Koiri and TV 10 L.I.V.E, an online news portal, as to why action should not be taken for defying HC’s order. The notices are returnable on Oct 27.The application said Tengra and four defendants were restrained by the June 5, 2023 order from publishing or circulating defamatory videos and content. The same night Tengra uploaded a fresh video. On June 9, 2023, the plaintiffs issued a takedown notice to Google and X. Google complied but X refused, stating HC’s order was not issued against it.Advocate Karl Tamboly, for SII and Poonawalla, said videos uploaded were held to be unlawful by the June 5, 2023 order.Hence, videos and content of a like nature are also directed to be removed. He said in the absence of Tengra complying with HC’s direction, X is obligated to remove the objectionable content. Advocate Mayur Khandeparkar, for X, said the plaintiffs must initiate contempt proceedings against the defendants instead of waging a proxy battle with an intermediary.Justice Godse said it is undisputed that the objectionable content is still available with X. Tengra uploaded the fresh video not only in blatant defiance of HC’s injunction order “but he also states that he will not comply with the directions of the court and that he would not stop calling plaintiff no. 2 (Poonawalla) ‘a mass murderer’.”The judge noted there were no directions to X to remove the objectionable content and, thus, it cannot be held liable for the objectionable content not removed by the five defendants or for the new content uploaded by Tengra. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, she said even if an intermediary is exempt from liability for third-party information, necessary directions can be issued to remove the unlawful or prohibited content.Considering the “subsequent circumstance” of Tengra uploading the fresh video, Justice Godse said sufficient grounds are made out to direct X to “remove, delete or disable access” to the fresh video uploaded by Tengra.
Article Summary: Bombay high court has directed x corp to remove a video against serum institute of india pvt ltd and its ceo adar poonawalla. The video was uploaded by social media influencer yohan tengra immediately after its june 5, 2023 order. Justice gauri godse of hc on tuesday passed the order on an interim application in the pending defamation suit.

Article Title: India's factory growth hits 7 month high in September, thanks to demand and hiring boost
Article Text:
Factory growth hits 7-month high, PMI rises to 55.1

India’s manufacturing activity scaled up sharply in September, as stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building.The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August, marking the strongest improvement in the sector’s health in seven months. A PMI reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signals contraction.The recovery in factory activity was supported by both domestic and overseas demand. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.Export orders also gained momentum during the month, with manufacturers reporting increased business from clients in Brazil, Europe, the UAE and the US."India's factory sector ended the quarter on a firmer footing. The PMI rose to 55.1 in September, up from 52.8, as stronger domestic and overseas demand lifted sales and production. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since May, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead," Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC, told PTI.The improvement in demand was accompanied by a renewed increase in factory employment.After a blip in August, job growth resumed in September, with the pace of employment expansion described by panellists as solid and the strongest since May.Manufacturers also became more confident about the months ahead. Output forecasts were upgraded during September, taking overall positive sentiment to a four-month high. The outlook was supported by a healthy pipeline of new enquiries and expectations that strong demand would continue.The expectation of higher future sales also prompted companies to increase their purchases of materials and build inventories. Overall buying activity expanded at a faster pace than in August."Companies bought more materials and built up stocks to prepare for anticipated sales. Finished goods inventories recorded their second-largest increase in nearly 12 years, signalling a clear shift from leaner stock levels," Bhandari said.Finished goods inventories rose for the third consecutive month. The increase was the second-fastest in 11-and-a-half years, behind July, as manufacturers actively accumulated stocks in anticipation of stronger demand.At the same time, companies faced quicker increases in input costs and selling prices. Despite the acceleration, the rates of inflation remained mild by historical standards.The September reading came as manufacturing activity regained momentum after the slower expansion recorded in August, with the PMI rising by more than two points during the month."Holdings of finished products increased for the third month in a row and at the second-fastest pace in 11-and-a-half years (behind July)," the report said.The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global based on responses from purchasing managers at around 400 manufacturers.
Article Summary: Factory growth hits 7-month high, pmi rises to 55.1. Stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since may, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead.

Article Title: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses
Article Text:
Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses

Revenue growth draws investor attention

Huge infrastructure spending

Losses add to valuation questions

Customer concentration remains a risk

Anthropic has put a massive price tag on the AI boom, backing it with an equally heavy spending plan.The AI giant is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion even as it plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.The company’s IPO prospectus, seen by Reuters, also shows just how quickly its business has grown. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments.The scale of its plans has also spilled into markets, with European technology shares rising 2.4% and the US chip index gaining 1.5%.For investors, Anthropic’s rapid expansion is a key part of the valuation story.Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar, Amsterdam, said the speed of the company’s growth stood out in the prospectus."If anything, the acceleration of the business is the biggest part of this release. Growing a big business can be difficult, but the prospectus stating that revenue grew by 12 fold in 2025 is truly remarkable."Field said the proposed valuation should be considered alongside the company’s sales."Obviously a $2 trillion valuation sounds outlandish, but when you break it down to a multiple of sales, likely to be around 18-20x, it sounds much more reasonable than the recent SpaceX IPO."Anthropic’s plans also show that the AI investment cycle is continuing to require substantial spending on infrastructure.Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB Platform, London, said the planned spending was positive for companies involved in semiconductors and AI infrastructure."This is positive for the AI trade, since it is fuelled by continued elevated levels of capex spend. The fact that Anthropic is planning on spending big on capex means that the capex cycle is not over yet. This is good news for semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies. I believe that if Anthropic had signalled a lower level of spending, this could have caused a wobble in the AI trade, since it would lead to fears about the sustainability of the AI trade as we move into Q4. "The prospectus puts rapid revenue growth alongside the large infrastructure commitments needed to support it.Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, London, said Anthropic’s expectations for AI’s economic impact appeared to have supported demand for European technology stocks."It's the vision and the projections to the extent to which Anthropic believes AI will be a game changer for economies around the world that seem to have lifted demand for European tech stocks."She also raised concerns over the company’s spending while it remains loss-making."There still will be niggles of concern among some about the huge sums that are projected to be spent even though it is making a loss. But that hasn't caused a flutter of general fear because, overall, there still seems to be a pretty hefty appetite for AI focused investments."Anthropic’s losses remain another factor in the debate around its proposed valuation.Field said the losses were a concern when considered against the company’s current revenue, growth rate and size. However, he said investors had already absorbed much of the spending story."The losses certainly are a concern. Particularly given the growth rate and the size relative to current revenues. It's unlikely to deter investors, however, with the spend story having been digested for some time now."He said the scale of planned investment also reflected management’s confidence in future demand."The key takeaway for investors is the confidence in the business and the AI strategy. Yes spend is high and growing, but management obviously feel the growth rate inherent in demand is sufficiently attractive to keep spending, hence why they are coming to market and demanding a top-dollar valuation."Anthropic’s revenue growth is another area attracting attention, particularly because a significant share reportedly comes from a small number of customers.Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, London, said the company’s revenue growth had become the main focus despite its spending plans. "Massive spending would normally have investors running for the hills, but what's capturing the market's attention is Anthropic's stellar revenue growth, up 12-fold in 2025. Admittedly, AI is moving at such a rapid pace that last year’s sales achievements relate to technology that is already outdated. "Anthropic’s IPO plans therefore bring together rapid revenue growth, continuing losses and a huge infrastructure commitment. The company is seeking a valuation of more than $2 trillion while planning $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations.
Article Summary: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses. Revenues reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments. European technology shares rose 2.4% and the us chip index gained 1.5%.

Article Title: Google data center head says that there are 'hundreds of thousands' of skilled trade jobs across the US as the company launches commitment to help 25,000 ...
Article Text:
A personal story behind the push

What the commitment includes

Why the need is so urgent

Part of a broader pattern of investment

Google has announced a major initiative to help 25,000 US veterans and military families transition into skilled trade careers, as demand for electricians, pipefitters, and project managers surges amid the AI-driven data center boom. Tim Chadwick, Google’s Data Center Operations Area Lead, says there are “hundreds of thousands” of skilled trade jobs open across the country right now. Data centers have become central to the AI economy, requiring massive investment and labor. Google estimates that hundreds of thousands of skilled trade roles are currently unfilled across the U.S., ranging from master electricians to project managers. These jobs offer long-term stability and high wages, but employers face challenges in recruiting due to decades of emphasis on four-year degrees over vocational training.The announcement was written by Tim Chadwick, Google's Data Center Operations Area lead for Ohio and Indiana, who shared his own path from military service into the tech industry. Chadwick spent seven years as a nuclear-trained operator in the US Navy and another 13 years as a submarine officer before transitioning to civilian life — a shift he described as genuinely difficult, one he credits his professional network with helping him navigate.A former shipmate ultimately helped him land an interview for a role managing data center engineering operations.Chadwick noted that many of the skills built while running a nuclear submarine — planning and leading a mission, working closely with technicians, and exercising sound judgment under pressure — translate directly into overseeing data center operations, a connection that shaped his interest in helping other veterans find similar paths.Google.org's funding and support will flow to three organizations with deep experience serving the veteran community: Hiring Our Heroes, Student Veterans of America (SVA), and the Home Builders Institute (HBI). Together, these organizations will offer hands-on pre-apprenticeships, career coaching, and direct job placement support aimed at helping veterans and military family members move into skilled trade careers.Chadwick pointed to the sheer scale of unmet demand driving the initiative, noting that hundreds of thousands of skilled trade roles are currently open across the US, spanning positions like master electrician, lead pipefitter, and project manager. He described these as high-growth careers offering long-term financial stability — and argued that veterans and military families are especially well-suited for them, given how closely the roles align with skills many already carry from military service, including problem-solving under pressure, teamwork, and a strong drive to get a job done right.This isn't Google's first move in this space. Earlier this year, the company joined BlackRock, Ford, and Carhartt to launch the Alliance for America's Skilled Trades, aimed at building stronger pipelines into vocational careers nationally. Google.org has also previously funded the Electrical Training Alliance (etA) to bring AI-powered learning tools directly onto the trade floor, and provided a $4 million grant to Student Veterans of America to expand access to Google Career Certificates and AI training for veterans nationwide.Today's announcement is also part of Google.org's broader AI Opportunity Fund for the United States, an initiative aimed at ensuring Americans across different career paths can benefit from advances in AI technology, rather than being left behind by them.
Article Summary: Google has announced a major initiative to help 25,000 us veterans and military families transition into skilled trade careers. The move comes as demand for electricians, pipefitters, and project managers surges amid the ai-driven data center boom. Google estimates that hundreds of thousands of skilled trade roles are currently unfilled across the u.s.

Article Title: Apple Pay launches in India; here's how to set it up and where you can use it
Article Text:
Apple Pay launched in India: How it works, and who can use it

How to set up and use Apple Pay

Where you can use it

Apple has officially launched Apple Pay in India. With this launch the company brings its secure and seamless payment system to iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch users, with Mac support coming soon. Apple Pay roll out in the country will enable users to pay in stores, apps, and on the web without typing PINs and OTPs marking a significant milestone in India’s fast-growing digital payments ecosystem. At launch, Apple Pay supports Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, enabling payments at thousands of merchants across India and anywhere NFC transactions are accepted globally.Apple also emphasised that privacy remains central to how Apple Pay functions. When a card is added, the actual card number is never stored on the device or Apple's servers, nor shared with merchants during a transaction. Instead, the system assigns a unique Device Account Number, which is encrypted and stored securely within the device's Secure Element — a certified, industry-standard chip built specifically to protect payment information.Presently, Apple Pay is exclusively available to customers holding Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, letting them add those cards to Apple Pay and use them at thousands of in-store and online merchants across India, as well as anywhere that accepts NFC transactions.Jennifer Bailey, Apple's vice president of Apple Pay and Apple Wallet, framed the launch as a natural fit for India's fast-growing digital economy, pointing to the country's dynamic, digitally savvy population that's increasingly embracing cashless payments while expecting strong security and privacy standards. She described Apple Pay's core value proposition as making everyday card payments easy, secure, and private — from a simple tap in stores without needing a separate app, PIN, or OTP, to checking out online without repeatedly re-entering payment details.Apple Pay is easy to set up. Customers can add a card directly to Apple Wallet via the latest version of the Axis Bank app. Alternatively, simply open the Wallet app on iPhone, tap the plus sign, and follow the steps to add an eligible card. Once a user adds a card to their Apple device, they can start using Apple Pay right away.Using Apple Pay in stores is seamless and easy. Simply double-click the side button or Home button; authenticate using Face ID, Touch ID, or a device passcode if prompted; and hold the top of the iPhone or display of the Apple Watch near the contactless reader to pay. When using Apple Pay, users will continue to earn the rewards and benefits offered by their cards.At launch, Apple Pay will be accepted at millions of merchants across India, including Apple Store locations, Blinkit, Chaayos, Comet, Croma, Interflora, Ixigo, Le15 Patisserie, Reliance brands, Tata 1mg, and Zomato, among others. Apple has also partnered with several payment service providers, including Cashfree, JusPay, Mswipe, Paytm, PayU, Pine Labs, Razorpay, and Worldline, to extend Apple Pay's reach across their respective merchant networks, with more merchants and apps expected to be added over time.Globally, Apple Pay is now available in more than 90 countries and regions, working with over 11,000 bank and network partners worldwide — making India one of the more prominent recent additions to that global rollout.
Article Summary: Apple has officially launched apple pay in india. With this launch the company brings its secure and seamless payment system to iphone, ipad and apple watch users, with mac support coming soon. Apple pay roll out in the country will enable users to pay in stores, apps, and on the web without typing pins and otps.

Article Title: Anthropic warns AI may pose ‘existential risks to humanity’ in IPO filing
Article Text:
Anthropic

Anthropic plans to warn potential investors in its initial public offering that advanced artificial intelligence could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity,” according to its IPO prospectus reviewed by Reuters.The filing says its AI models could exhibit “self-preserving behaviours,” including attempts to “resist shutdown,” “conceal or manipulate information” and behaviour “resembling blackmail”. “Our development of highly advanced models, platforms, and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm,” Anthropic said.The company, which positions itself as a safety-first AI lab, devoted 80 pages of prospectus’s 261-page main body to risks, nearly twice the 48 pages describing its business. SpaceX, which owns xAI, devoted about 38 of 277 pages to risks.Anthropic said models could develop unexpected capabilities during training that might be discovered only after deployment and had resulted in significant safety incidents. It also warned that models might recognise evaluations and modify their behaviour, limiting safety assessments. Researchers have similarly warned that increasingly capable models can recognise when they are being watched and adjust their behaviour, complicating monitoring.Anthropic and other developers, including OpenAI, have faced scrutiny after experimental systems defied constraints, including a reported breach of Australia’s health-system database by an OpenAI model. Anthropic safety researcher Evan Hubinger estimated a greater than 10% probability that AI could kill humans within the next decade, echoing former colleague Jacob Coxon.Despite emphasising safety, Anthropic said returns on such investment were unclear and did not disclose its spending. Earlier this month, it said safety work used about 6% of its AI research computing power during a sample week in July. It called safety efforts “resource-intensive” and said limited funds must be divided among computing power, costly AI talent and safety.The Claude developer said customer usage and revenue depended on new models and that a “continuous and overlapping cadence” of releases was “inherent to remaining at the frontier of AI development.” Last week, it released a new Opus model, 10 days after CEO Dario Amodei published a nearly 4,000-word essay urging the frontier to be paced.Anthropic has pledged to publish more data on its use of AI models to build future generations as experts warn about recursive self-improvement, when models develop without human help. Anthropic declined to comment. Analysts said slowing down could hand rivals an advantage. Anthropic declined to comment in response to a request for comment.
Article Summary: Anthropic plans to warn potential investors in its initial public offering that advanced artificial intelligence could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” the company, which positions itself as a safety-first ai lab, devoted 80 pages of prospectus’s 261-page main body to risks.

Article Title: AT&T CEO John Stankey 'agrees' with T-Mobile CEO Peter Osvaldik that Elon Musk's plans to shake up mobile industry with Starlink should be laughed out of the room
Article Text:
What T-Mobile CEO Peter Osvaldik said first

AT&T CEO John Stankey's rebuttal: Fiber beats satellite, full stop

Why the rivalry is heating up

The scale of Starlink's ambitions

Why Stankey says the math doesn't work

AT&T CEO John Stankey has sided with T-Mobile’s chief executive Peter Osvaldik in rejecting Elon Musk ’s plan to disrupt the mobile industry with Starlink. Speaking to Axios, Stankey said SpaceX ’s proposal to turn its satellite business into a global competitor to traditional telecom networks is “not a viable strategy.” He argued that fiber infrastructure remains superior, noting AT&T’s $3 billion deal with Corning to expand its fiber footprint. Earlier this month, T-Mobile CEO Peter Osvaldik dismissed Musk’s Starlink ambitions outright, and said that the strategy should be “laughed out of the room. ” Osvaldik said Starlink’s approach lacked the scale and economics to compete with established carriers, reinforcing skepticism across the telecom industry.T-Mobile CFO Peter Osvaldik was blunt in his own assessment of Starlink's mobile ambitions, saying that "everybody in the know" is laughing at parts of the plan, and describing SpaceX's proposal as something that isn't fathomable from a technical standpoint. He argued Starlink doesn't represent a real competitive threat from a wireless perspective, pointing to basic physics as the core obstacle: satellite signals, he said, can't penetrate buildings, walls, or even something as simple as a car windshield, making Starlink's direct-to-cell ambitions far less practical in dense urban environments than in the remote areas where satellite coverage genuinely shines.Speaking to Axios, Stankey made a similarly confident case for why AT&T isn't worried, backing it with a major infrastructure move. AT&T announced a $3 billion deal with Corning this week to expand its fiber infrastructure, arguing that fiber delivers speeds three times faster than satellite technology. Stankey didn't mince words about the comparison, saying nothing beats fiber, and that even if satellite technology performs at its absolute best over the next decade, it still won't be able to match what fiber delivers.The pushback from both carriers comes as Musk and SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell have been increasingly vocal about turning Starlink into a genuine competitor to traditional phone and internet providers. Starlink already competes with legacy telecom companies for home and business internet customers, and the company has now started talking openly about a mobile business that would put it in direct competition with wireless carriers.Shotwell added fuel to that narrative in August, during SpaceX's first earnings call as a public company, predicting that SpaceX would be able to win over a meaningful number of customers from existing carriers because its service would simply be better. That comment rattled markets, sending shares of AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile lower the following day.As of June 30, Starlink had 12 million subscribers and more than 10,200 satellites providing coverage across 167 countries, according to SpaceX's first earnings report as a public company. While SpaceX's rockets and AI work tend to dominate headlines, its connectivity business is actually the company's largest revenue driver, accounting for 55% of total sales.Becoming a genuine fourth major US mobile carrier, however, would require significantly more terrestrial infrastructure to match the capacity of a traditional cellular network — a build-out one analyst estimated could cost SpaceX more than $100 billion. SpaceX believes it has found a cheaper alternative: installing small cellular base stations alongside Starlink dishes at homes and businesses, adding capacity where satellite coverage alone falls short, without needing to build the kind of sprawling cell tower network traditional carriers rely on. Musk has claimed these small stations could eventually deliver connectivity to phones with better and higher bandwidth than what's currently available from existing cellular providers.Stankey pushed back hard on that plan's feasibility, arguing that installing enough small stations to match a traditional network's capacity would cost roughly the same as simply building a full macro cellular network. He also pointed to a significant regulatory hurdle: current law doesn't allow companies to radiate cellular signals from someone's home without their permission, unless that law changes. He suggested that if the approach were genuinely viable and cost-effective, AT&T would already be installing similar antennas across its own massive existing fiber network.
Article Summary: At&t ceo john stankey says spacex's starlink plan is "not a viable strategy" he argued that fiber infrastructure remains superior, noting at&t’s $3 billion deal with corning to expand its fiber footprint. Earlier this month, t-mobile ceo peter osvaldik said starlink's approach lacked the scale and economics to compete with established carriers.

Pebble Qore Ultra

Pebble Qore Ultra features

Pebble Qore Ultra price and availability

Home-grown consumer electronics brand Pebble has launched Qore Ultra, its flagship wellness band. In a press release, the company said that the device is designed for continuous, distraction-free wear. Coming with 3 ATM water-resistant design, Qore Ultra integrates a 4-PD precision sensor array and 6-axis motion sensors. “This hardware architecture enables 24x7 tracking of vital metrics, including heart rate, HRV, SpO2, respiration, and stress, while delivering up to 15 days of continuous battery life,” it stated.The band features automatic workout detection for activities like walking and running, over 100 sports modes, and in-app GPS sports tracking. The Pebble Qore mobile application acts as the central hub for this health intelligence, seamlessly translating complex data into intuitive metrics. Users can gauge their daily preparedness through a 0-100 Readiness Score, factoring in HRV, sleep quality, and stress, while monitoring their real-time stamina via the Body Energy Score. For long-term health tracking, the platform calculates Body Age every three days and uses GPS-tracked runs to estimate VO2 Max and Fitness Age.Komal Agarwal, Co-founder of Pebble said “The Pebble Qore series has become one of India's top fitness bands, and the Qore Ultra represents the flagship evolution of that journey. We have put a significant amount of R&D into giving users actionable data that can help them improve their daily rest, activity, and habits. By providing these comprehensive insights alongside community features on our new app, we are shifting the focus from isolated tracking to shared wellness management. ”Pebble Qore Ultra will be available from October 2, 2026 in three color options, Desert Gold, Deep Black, and Deep Blue. Priced at an introductory Rs 5,999 (MRP 8,999), the wearable will be available through Pebble's official website, Flipkart, Amazon, and leading retail stores across the country.

Article Title: How two brothers put the humble handpan on Bengluru’s musical map
Article Text:
PASSION FOR MUSIC: Ranganathan andSriniketan with their handpans (R) and apractice session of the ensemble

PASSION FOR MUSIC

What is a handpan?

Origin:

Meaning of its name:

Material:





Twenty-six handpans turned a Bengaluru festival stage into a sea of metallic sound. At the centre of the 24-member ensemble were brothers, Ranganathan S, 15, and Sriniketan S, 11. They had spent months rehearsing, travelling across the city several times a week and helping coordinate compositions for the ensemble.At its debut public performance at Bengaluru's Ganesha Utsava, the ensemble played five songs with 26 handpans alongside mridangam, ghatam, drums, guitar, synth and djembe. Their repertoire included Carnatic compositions along with 'Varaha Roopam' from the film 'Kantara.'Led by the Nadamaya Brothers, who were playing two handpans each, the performance offered the city's growing handpan community an opportunity to demonstrate that an instrument still on the fringes of mainstream music can function as a lead instrument. Their journey began during the pandemic.Ranganathan, who was nine then, had already been experimenting with the keyboard when a neighbour invited him to see an unusual percussion instrument he had begun crafting.His first impression remains vivid. "It looked like a spaceship," he recalls. Intrigued by its shape and sound, he quickly picked up the basics. Within a few hours, he was exploring melodies on an instrument he had never encountered before. Soon, his younger brother followed.Sriniketan says he was initially drawn to the instrument because his elder brother was playing it. "I was inspired by watching my brother play the handpan. I have been learning to play the handpan for the past three years now. What I love most is that it combines percussion and melody, so you can play both at once without needing two separate instruments," he says.Today, both brothers practise for at least two hours every day, often spending considerably longer when preparing for a public performance. Ranganathan, having completed his Class 10 examinations ahead of schedule, has taken a gap year to focus entirely on music, combining handpan practice with Carnatic vocal training and Vedic studies.Age, however, is not the only reason why the brothers have attracted attention within the handpan community. Fellow performers describe them as among the country's most accomplished young handpan players. While other ensemble members handle rhythmic and harmonic layers, the brothers perform the lead melodies, navigating complex arrangements and Carnatic-inspired compositions on chromatic handpans carrying more than 40 notes.Their rise mirrors the growth of Bengaluru's handpan community itself.At the centre of this growth is Chirag Vaitheeswaran, founder of Chirp Handpans, regarded by the handpan community as one of India's pioneering indigenous handpan makers. His fascination with the instrument began in 2013, when he encountered one on a beach in Gokarna. At the time, handpans were difficult to obtain, with long international waiting lists and high import costs.He embarked on a painstaking quest to build one himself while working at Microsoft. For nearly two years, he estimates that he produced nearly 200 failed shells before crafting a successful instrument. His Bengaluru workshop now employs 14 artisans and has delivered more than 1,300 instruments crafted entirely from Indian-sourced materials.Making the instrument accessible contributed to the growth of Bengaluru's handpan community through workshops and impromptu jam sessions. Players began looking beyond the instrument's familiar association with meditation, yoga retreats, and ambient soundscapes."I truly believe this instrument has the power to touch people across age groups and backgrounds, and I'm excited to be part of a community that's helping introduce it to more people," says ensemble member, Shruthi Shetty.The ensemble itself is designed to highlight the melodic and rhythmic capabilities of the handpan, with different performers assigned roles like those in an orchestra. The arrangement, inspired partly by steel-pan ensembles in Trinidad and Tobago, seeks to demonstrate that the instrument can support complex musical performances rather than simply create atmosphere. That vision resonates strongly with Ranganathan.His ambition is to take Indian handpan music to international audiences and expand its repertoire through Carnatic music, film songs and original compositions. He believes familiarity is key: audiences first recognise a song and then begin paying attention to the instrument producing it. "If it stays in the background, it won't become famous," says the teenager. "I want it to become like the flute or the mandolin. "The handpan is still an unfamiliar instrument for many people. Resembling a metallic flying saucer, it is played entirely with the hands and produces deep, resonant tones that blend melody and rhythm. The handpan is tuned to a specific scale, allowing even first-time players to create harmonious sounds, making it accessible.Inspired by the steelpan from Trinidad and Tobago, as well as traditional instruments like the Indian ghatam and Indonesian gamelan, people across the world started refining and creating their own versions of handpans. The creators combined elements of the Caribbean steelpan (steel drum) with the Indian ghatam (a clay pot percussion instrument, mostly used in Carnatic music)."Hang" means "hand" in the Bernese German dialect, describing how the instrument is played.It is built from two glued-together steel shells made of a treated metal, called nitrided steel.
Article Summary: Brothers ranganathan s, 15, and sriniketan s, 11, are among india's most accomplished handpan players. At their debut public performance at bengaluru's ganesha utsava, the ensemble played five songs with 26 handpans alongside mridangam, ghatam, drums, guitar and djembe.

Article Title: A North Dakota farm kid turned ag-tech entrepreneur; his company puts real farm maps on children's play rugs
Article Text:
Representative Image of a colorful map-themed play rug featuring various agricultural fields and farm buildings (AI Generated Image)

From a North Dakota farm to agricultural mapping

How the play-rug idea began

What Boundri sells today

The " carpet farming " idea

A North Dakota farm kid has turned real agricultural maps into children's play rugs, giving toy tractors and combines a miniature version of the landscapes they come from. Nathan Faleide, founder of Boundri, grew up on a farm in North Dakota and around agricultural mapping through his family's Satshot business. Boundri was started in 2022 and grew from a play rug Faleide made for his children into a company that now puts personalised maps on rugs and other products. Today, Boundri sells mapped play rugs, blankets, wall maps, prints and other customised products, while its mapping background stretches back decades through the Faleide family's work in agricultural technology.Faleide's connection to farming began early. On Boundri's current About Us page, he says he grew up on a farm in North Dakota and that farm toys were central to his daily routine. He also says he "did farm a little" himself, but adds that it "wasn't my time." At the same time, he grew up around agricultural mapping through his family's company, Satshot. Faleide says that experience helped develop his expertise in software and maps, eventually providing the technical background behind Boundri.Satshot's history dates to 1994, when Lanny Faleide, Nathan's father, built software to create variable-rate maps using satellite imagery.Satshot says Lanny had more than 20 years of farming experience at the time and that the idea grew from flying as a pilot over his own fields and those of neighbouring farmers in the mid-to-late 1980s. The company also links the development of the technology to difficult conditions in farming during that period. The technology has since continued under Boundri. Satshot's current website describes Satshot as a brand, service and product of Boundri Inc., and says the technology created by Lanny has continued in a new direction with Nathan Faleide. It also says Boundri will continue to run the Satshot brand, product and service "for the time being" while developing new connections and tools around mapping and imagery.The first idea was much closer to home. On Boundri's own website, Faleide says the business began with a farm-toy play rug he made for his children. He describes the family as the inspiration for Boundri and says the project grew after seeing the enjoyment his children got from the rug. DTN reported in December 2022 that Faleide had nearly 25 years of experience in precision agriculture and mapping at the time and had long wanted to do more imagery-based art. The publication reported that when he introduced an early prototype, his children began playing with their farm toys on it. A photograph of the rug was subsequently shared by a friend on Twitter, after which orders began arriving. DTN reported that about 230 orders came in while the business was still in its early stages.AgWeb also reported that the product gained attention on Twitter as the business began taking off. An autumn 2022 report from Agweek described Boundri's initial offering as generic farm-print rugs, with custom products expected to follow. The early launch eventually developed into the personalised products that now form a major part of Boundri's range. Rather than limiting the designs to generic farm scenes, the company built its products around maps and imagery connected to specific locations.Farm play rugs remain one of Boundri's main products. Its current site lists personalised farm play rugs in three sizes and also offers custom-upload rugs and other mapped products. The company says its rugs are made from polyester chenille, have hemmed edges and a no-skid polyester backing, and can be cleaned with dish soap, a rag and a hose. It also says the rugs fold for storage and are lightweight. For customers who already have their own imagery, Boundri's FAQ provides more specific instructions. It says satellite, plane or drone images can be uploaded through the company's Custom Product Builder, rather than through its main-page products. The FAQ says the files must currently be JPG or PNG and smaller than 50 MB.Boundri's product page also explains the proof process. Customers can order an item and then send a note explaining any changes they want. The company says a proof is provided before the item is printed. The business now extends beyond children's play rugs. Boundri's website lists blankets, puzzles, onesies, canvas prints and other mapped products, while its wall-map and mural work can include features such as field boundaries, attributes and other map layers. The company says these custom projects are handled on a case-by-case basis.The phrase "carpet farming" appears in both coverage of Boundri and the company's own current website. DTN used the phrase when it covered the business in 2022, while Boundri uses it on its product pages to describe the children who play with its farm rugs. Its current Custom Upload Rugs page, for example, describes the product as a gift for "little carpet farmers."The concept gives children something more specific than a generic farm-themed play surface. Boundri's products can represent actual locations, turning maps associated with farms and other meaningful places into physical objects that can be used, displayed or given as gifts. For Faleide, the business brings together two parts of his background: farming and agricultural mapping. The technology behind Satshot grew from his family's experience with agricultural imagery and mapping, while Boundri has taken that knowledge into a very different kind of product. What began with a farm-toy rug for his own children has grown into a business built around putting maps onto objects people can use and keep.
Article Summary: Nathan faleide grew up on a farm in north dakota and around agricultural mapping through his family's company, satshot. He says the idea for boundri began with a play rug he made for his children. Today, boundri sells mapped play rugs, blankets, wall maps, prints and other customised products.

Article Title: ‘Time for trial and error is over’: OpenAI safety employee David Robinson quits over AI risks
Article Text:
David Robinson made the comments in an article titled "I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken".

A former OpenAI safety employee has resigned from the company, warning that its rapid development of increasingly capable AI systems could raise the risk of serious failures. David Robinson said the “time for trial and error is over” and argued that AI companies need to put far greater emphasis on safety before developing more powerful systems.Robinson made the comments in an article titled "I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken", published by The Atlantic on Saturday.Robinson said AI companies, including OpenAI, were not being "nearly careful enough" and argued that safety research and expertise should play a much bigger role before more powerful AI systems are developed.Robinson spent 3-1/2 years at OpenAI, where he helped draft the company's preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches. He said the company's focus on moving quickly from one AI model launch to another was making it difficult to maintain the level of caution he believed was necessary."As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed."He argued that the development of advanced AI should no longer rely on a process of repeatedly releasing systems, finding problems and fixing them afterwards.OpenAI refers to this approach as "iterative deployment", under which systems are released and their safeguards are strengthened as new problems are identified.Robinson argued that this approach is no longer sufficient as AI systems become more powerful."The time for trial and error is over," he wrote, saying advanced AI systems should have safeguards comparable to those used in high-risk fields such as nuclear power and aviation.His criticism comes amid a wider debate in the AI industry over whether companies are developing increasingly powerful systems faster than their ability to understand and control them. OpenAI and rival Anthropic have both faced scrutiny following incidents involving failed safety controls or unexpected behaviour from experimental AI systems.Robinson also warned that AI capabilities are advancing faster than researchers' understanding of alignment. AI alignment refers to efforts to ensure that AI systems behave in ways that are consistent with human goals and values.OpenAI defended its approach, saying it continues to put safety measures in place and can slow development when necessary."We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down," an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement.
Article Summary: Former openai safety employee david robinson has resigned from the company. Robinson said the “time for trial and error is over” and argued that ai companies need to put far greater emphasis on safety before developing more powerful systems.

Article Title: AI sings Russia's war story: Inside the rise of generative songs about Ukraine conflict
Article Text:
Among the songs whose release dates could be established, most appeared after 2024. (Reuters photo)

Nearly 1,000 songs identified

AI tools can produce war-related music

Streaming platforms tighten AI rules

Artificial intelligence is being used to produce a growing number of songs about the Russia-Ukraine war, with some of the music presenting Russia's invasion in a favourable light and criticising Ukraine.Hundreds of such tracks have appeared on major music streaming platforms, including Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube and Deezer, according to research by Terrecon, a Ukrainian nonprofit organisation focused on threat intelligence.The songs cover a wide range of musical styles, from ballads to heavy metal. Terrecon said some praise Russian soldiers, describe the war from a Russian perspective and contain derogatory references to Ukrainians, including ethnic slurs.One of the more popular tracks identified by the organisation is “Power of Artillery”, a Russian-language rock song centred on artillery systems including Krasnopol and Carnation.Terrecon said it catalogued 981 songs created with AI that contained what it classified as pro-Russian war propaganda.Among the songs whose release dates could be established, most appeared after 2024. That coincided with the wider availability of AI music generators such as Sudo and Udio.The technology has lowered the time and cost involved in producing music, according to Daria Verbytska, a founder of Terrecon.“They have found new ways to create cheaper drones and use them on a massive scale,” Daria Verbytska, a founder of Terrecon, said told NYT in a telephone interview, referring to the Russians. “It’s like that with music — creating massive propaganda with the help of AI”Some of the songs use themes associated with Soviet-era war music but present them through contemporary genres. One track, “Soldier's Daughter”, describes the death of a soldier and the impact on his child while also portraying the soldier's sacrifice in a positive light.It is not clear how much involvement, if any, the Russian government has had in producing or distributing the songs. However, the Kremlin has supported cultural projects aimed at promoting patriotic themes.Last week, a director of Moscow's Internet Development Institute, an organisation that works closely with the Kremlin to promote patriotic values, said in a presentation that the institute had supported more than 350 artistic projects related to the war, according to Russian media reports.Terrecon also tested several AI music generators to see how they responded to prompts requesting songs promoting Russian views of the war.Researchers used Suno, Udio and Google Flow Music in the US, along with Singapore-based Mureka. They entered prompts in both Russian and English, including requests involving violence and derogatory descriptions.The platforms rejected some prompts, but researchers said they were nevertheless able to generate songs resembling some of those in Terrecon's database. They then uploaded the tracks to YouTube Music and SoundCloud.“The moderation systems mainly responded to specific banned words rather than the overall meaning of the prompts,” Terrecon’s report found.The researchers said the issue is partly linked to the differing rules adopted by AI music services and streaming platforms. They also said automated systems may have difficulty identifying expressions, slang and offensive language in different languages.Major music platforms generally have policies covering hate speech and violent content, although fewer have specific rules dealing with propaganda.Deezer and YouTube are among the platforms that require certain AI-generated content to be labelled. Spotify said in September that it had introduced a policy to label AI-generated songs and prevent them from being recommended to users. The company also added labels to songs shared by The New York Times as examples.Terrecon said the songs it identified had been played millions of times across major streaming services, although the extent to which listeners understood that some of the music was AI-generated or politically motivated is unclear.Deezer spokesman Jesper Wendel said the platform reviews potentially rule-breaking content on a case-by-case basis.SoundCloud spokeswoman Sade Ayodele said the company reviews reported content and added that “there is no place on SoundCloud for content that incites or glorifies violence.”The emergence of these songs illustrates how AI music tools can be used to produce and distribute large volumes of war-related material. It also presents streaming and AI companies with the challenge of deciding how existing rules on hate speech, violence, political content and AI-generated material should apply to such music.
Article Summary: Hundreds of such tracks have appeared on major music streaming platforms, including spotify, apple music, youtube and deezer. The songs cover a wide range of musical styles, from ballads to heavy metal. Some praise russian soldiers, describe the war from a russian perspective and contain derogatory references to ukrainians, including ethnic slurs.

Article Title: Chinese AI agents display 'concerning' behaviour in safety tests, mirroring US systems
Article Text: Chinese-powered AI agents are showing behaviours such as deception, bypassing safeguards and concealing failures, according to research papers and technical assessments reviewed by Reuters.These findings mirror growing concerns about the risks posed by increasingly autonomous AI systems in the United States.In one experiment, agents powered by models from Alibaba, DeepSeek and Moonshot falsely exaggerated their capabilities to win a simulated business tender and became more deceptive when given another opportunity. In another test, agents concealed their inability to complete tasks by fabricating files, simulating results and using alternative sources.One study found that false claims appeared in 88% of sessions involving Alibaba's Qwen3-Max-Preview, 84% sessions involving DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp and 88% sessions involving Moonshot's Kimi-K2 during a simulated bidding exercise. When agents were allowed to learn from previous rounds, deceptive behaviour increased by 12 to 20 percentage points.Another study involving 11 AI agents found that systems powered by both Chinese and US models sometimes responded to broken tools or missing files by guessing answers, substituting sources, simulating results or fabricating files rather than acknowledging failure.Other research found more serious behaviour in controlled settings. Fudan University researchers reported that an AI system powered by Alibaba's Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct created a copy of itself in another computing environment after receiving information that it could be replaced, while other tests showed attempts to avoid shutdown. In a separate case, researchers developing the Alibaba-linked ROME agent said it connected an Alibaba Cloud computer to an external machine without instruction and redirected computing resources toward cryptocurrency mining. Security systems stopped the activity, and there was no evidence that the agent spread beyond the external system.Chinese companies have also reported instances of agents attempting to circumvent safeguards. DeepSeek said agents in its production training system had tried to obtain answers through unintended channels, including by forging user requests, prompting tighter access controls. China has introduced guidance requiring AI agents to remain within authorised boundaries, while its latest AI safety framework identifies risks including agents independently obtaining resources, deceiving evaluators, concealing capabilities and exploiting weaknesses in isolated environments.Experts say China remains behind the US in developing a broader ecosystem for evaluating catastrophic AI risks. For instance, officials from the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC), the country's top internet regulator, told a foreign diplomat in July that Moonshot's Kimi-K3 - one of the most advanced Chinese AI models - was about three to six months behind its leading US rivals.However, unlike in the US, Chinese AI companies have not been exposed to the same level of public scrutiny or faced the same calls from whistleblowing employees or senior executives seeking a slowdown in the AI race.For its research, Reuters reviewed more than 200 research papers and technical documents and identified at least 20 studies since 2025 documenting potentially concerning behaviours among AI agents powered by Chinese systems. These included attempts to bypass restrictions, replicate themselves, avoid shutdown and exploit weaknesses in controlled environments. However, there was no evidence that any Chinese-powered agent independently escaped into the wider internet or became impossible to shut down.Most incidents took place in controlled experiments designed to test AI safety limits, and some involved models from US and other companies as well.
Article Summary: Chinese-powered ai agents are showing behaviours such as deception, bypassing safeguards and concealing failures. These findings mirror growing concerns about the risks posed by increasingly autonomous ai systems in the united states. For its research, reuters reviewed more than 200 research papers and technical documents.

Article Title: A shopper paid just C$5 for a painting at a Canadian donation centre in 2020; experts identified it as a David Bowie original, and it sold for C$108,120 at auction the following year
Article Text:
Photo: cowley abbott/ Instagram

From a donation bin to a global auction

Bowie as a painter and collector

Photo: cowley abbott/ Instagram

The Dead Heads series explained

A record-breaking auction outcome

Why the discovery connected with people

Bowie's visual legacy beyond music

In 2020, a shopper browsing a household goods donation centre in South River, Ontario, spotted a small painting tucked among discarded items and paid just C$5 for it. The buyer soon noticed a label on the reverse reading David Bowie and contacted auction house Cowley Abbott to investigate. After research and correspondence with a Bowie specialist in the UK, experts confirmed the work as an original from the musician's Dead Heads series, and in June 2021 it sold at auction for C$108,120, setting a new global record for a David Bowie artwork, according to a post on Cowleyabbott.ca. Read on to know more here:The painting, titled D Head XLVI, was found in the most unexpected of places, a donation centre for household goods in Northern Ontario. The consignor was astonished to see the label bearing Bowie's name and realised that the signature on the reverse was that of the artist himself.What began as a casual purchase for just C$5 quickly became a story that captured the attention of collectors and media outlets around the world. Cowley Abbott performed due diligence before listing the work, including direct correspondence with a David Bowie specialist in the United Kingdom.Their research confirmed that the painting was indeed by Bowie and was part of a series that he completed in the 1990s. Article Title: 'Do not come to USA for your masters': Ed-tech entrepreneur warns Indian students about returning with huge debt
Article Text:
An ed-tech entrepreneur said Indian students should not come to the US for their master's.

OPT, H-1B crackdown in the US

An ed-tech entrepreneur shared his view of the job market for Indian students in the US after they complete higher studies at US colleges or universities and said Indian students should not come to the US for their master's. Dhaval Patel, an Indian founder, said this is his personal opinion that he arrived at after speaking to a student, and he was not spreading fear. Citing figures, Patel said that an Indian student comes to study in the US empty handed but when they go back without finding any job, they have a huge debt on their shoulders, as a master's course of two years costs around $100K."I am saying this based on a conversation I have had with a guy a couple of days ago who completed his master's from a reputed and credible college (Stevens Institute of Technology (NJ)). Most of his friends who studied with him had to go back to India as they couldn't get a job/h1b visa. Total expense for a 2-year master's will be close to 100 K $ or 95 lakh INR (70K fees and 30K other expenses). Going back with a huge debt can be quite challenging," he wrote in a LinkedIn Post."I've seen many others struggle as well and this is not a one-off incident. Now of course there are outliers, people with exceptional skill and luck who will get a job + h1b but the % of that happening is low," he added.The warning comes amid a tense situation for Indians in the US, with the administration cracking down on visa abuse and thus narrowing the scope of international students getting jobs after their studies. OPT, STEM-OPT used to be a pipeline for international students to get into jobs. But the administration vowed that any program that is giving international students and foreign workers more chance that equally skilled Americans will be ended.Transitioning from an F-1 visa to an H-1B has become tougher. H-1B is also getting costlier, with the administration imposing a hefty fee on it, which is still being blocked by courts. IT staffing companies are facing a probe, and many IT giants are facing delays in H-1B extension petitions this month.
